Here’s a classic, fool‑proof list of ingredients for a moist, chocolate‑y cake that’s perfect for birthdays, parties, or a cozy Sunday treat. Feel free to tweak quantities or add extras (like espresso powder or a splash of orange liqueur) to suit your taste. | Ingredient | Quantity (for a 9‑inch round cake, 2 layers) | Notes | |------------|---------------------------------------------|-------| | All‑purpose flour | 1 ¾ cups (220 g) | Sifted, or sift and then whisk in to avoid lumps. | | Unsweetened cocoa powder | ¾ cup (75 g) | Use a high‑quality Dutch‑process cocoa for richer flavor. | | Granulated sugar | 2 cups (400 g) | White sugar gives a clean sweetness; you can swap half for brown sugar for a deeper flavor. | | Baking powder | 1 ½ tsp | Helps the cake rise; make sure it’s fresh. | | Baking soda | 1 ½ tsp | Works with the acidity of the cocoa and buttermilk. | | Salt | ½ tsp | Enhances all the flavors. | | Buttermilk (or 1 ½ cups milk + 1 ½ tbsp lemon juice, set 5 min) | 1 ½ cups (360 ml) | Adds moisture and a slight tang that balances the chocolate. | | Eggs | 2 large | Room‑temperature for better emulsion. | | Vegetable oil (or melted butter) | ½ cup (120 ml) | Oil keeps the cake tender; butter adds richness if you prefer. | | Vanilla extract | 2 tsp | Pure vanilla for depth. | | Boiling water | 1 cup (240 ml) | Hot water dissolves cocoa and flour, creating a silky batter. | | Optional extras | | • 1–2 tbsp espresso powder (boosts chocolate flavor)
• ½ cup chocolate chips or chunks (for extra texture)
• ¼ cup chopped nuts (walnuts, pecans) | ### Quick Prep Tips 1. **Preheat** your oven to 350 °F (175 °C). No need to pre‑heat the pan—just the oven. 2. **Grease** and flour two 9‑inch round cake pans (or line with parchment circles). 3. **Mix dry ingredients** together in a bowl; whisk to combine. 4. **Whisk wet ingredients** (buttermilk, eggs, oil, vanilla) in another bowl. 5. **Combine** wet and dry mixtures, then fold in the boiling water (the batter will be thin—this is normal). 6. **Bake** 25–30 min per layer, or until a toothpick comes out clean. 7. **Cool** in the pans for 10 min, then turn onto a wire rack to cool completely before frosting. Enjoy your chocolate cake! If you’d like a specific frosting or glaze recipe, just let me know.
